experiment: FoundationStereo zero-shot reproduction and KITTI fine-tuning with Middlebury retention check

metrics.kitti: EPE = pixel-weighted mean absolute disparity error (px). D1 = % of pixels with error > 3 px AND > 5% of GT (global = pixel-weighted; mean_image = average of per-image D1). 'all' = disp_occ GT, 'noc' = disp_noc GT.
metrics.middlebury: Eval3 trainingH (15 scenes), half resolution, non-occluded pixels (mask0nocc == 255). EPE (px) and BP-2 = % of pixels with error > 2 px, pixel-weighted over all scenes.
metrics.inference: valid_iters = 32, mixed precision, no extra downscaling

fine_tuning_setup.trainable: all layers except the DINOv2 backbone (frozen)
fine_tuning_setup.optimizer: AdamW, lr 1e-5, weight decay 1e-5, grad clip 1.0
fine_tuning_setup.loss: Smooth-L1 over all GRU iterations, gamma 0.9 weighting, train_iters 12
fine_tuning_setup.validation: every 50 steps, early stopping after 3 evaluations without improvement

protocol_a.description: Cross-dataset: train on KITTI 2012, validate and test on disjoint KITTI 2015 splits

protocol_b.description: Train and validate on KITTI 2012 only, test on all of KITTI 2015 (KITTI 2015 never seen)

findings: Zero-shot Middlebury BP-2 of 1.10% reproduces the paper's ~1.1%.
KITTI fine-tuning cuts KITTI 2015 D1-all by 35-40% within a few hundred steps (best checkpoint at step 350 for Protocol A).
Both KITTI-adapted models roughly double Middlebury BP-2 (1.10% -> ~2.4%): domain adaptation costs zero-shot generalization even with DINOv2 frozen.
Protocol B (never saw KITTI 2015) is slightly better on KITTI 2015 than Protocol A; test sets differ (200 vs 160 pairs), so this is indicative, not a strict comparison.
Forgetting on Middlebury is essentially the same for both protocols, so the cause is the shift to the KITTI domain itself, not which split was used.
